lines: A typo should not cost you the form. Now Join tells you what to fix.
Leave out your name, mistype your email, or choose a short password, and the form names each field, and sends nothing.
The summary takes focus, and each link moves you to its field. Fix one, and its message clears.
If that email already has an account, in any mix of capitals, the email field says so, with a way to sign in instead.
If the server refuses, or does not answer, a message says so, and everything you typed stays.
The API checks the same rules again. It answers four hundred with a code and each field, or four oh nine for a taken email.
One table of rules runs in both stacks, row for row, and two joins racing for one email get the same answer.
And a name that holds markup is shown as the characters you typed, never as HTML.
Every test failed first. Now they all pass.
Next, slice three point one: sign in and sign out.
That's slice two point two. Christian Fitness: a Christian community for health in body and spirit.
